objective: Read EXPLAIN output to tell a sequential scan from an index scan, and recognize filters that cannot use an index
secondaryObjectives: Explain how a B-tree index speeds lookups and range scans and what it costs on writes and storage

sources.note: Relevant text: scan nodes 'return raw rows from a table'; a sequential scan with a WHERE clause 'checks the condition for each row it scans, and outputs only the ones that pass'; an Index Scan shows 'Index Cond'; with ANALYZE, 'EXPLAIN actually executes the query' and 'Rows Removed by Filter' counts rows a filter rejected. Read through a summarizing fetch of the PostgreSQL 18.7 page on 2026-11-14. The plan lines in the scenario are authored renderings in EXPLAIN's style; the costs and times are invented for the case.

Relevant text: 'a common way to do case-insensitive comparisons is to use the lower function: SELECT * FROM test1 WHERE lower(col1) = 'value'; This query can use an index if one has been defined on the result of the lower(col1) function'; index expressions 'are relatively expensive to maintain' on insert and update. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Why the existing index on email cannot serve a filter on lower(email).

sources.cite: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, CREATE INDEX (Building Indexes Concurrently)
sources.note: Relevant text: 'Normally PostgreSQL locks the table to be indexed against writes ... Other transactions can still read the table, but if they try to insert, update, or delete rows in the table they will block until the index build is finished.' With CONCURRENTLY PostgreSQL 'will build the index without taking any locks that prevent concurrent inserts, updates, or deletes', at the cost of two table scans; it 'cannot' run inside a transaction block, and a failed build leaves an 'invalid' index to drop and rebuild. Read through a summarizing fetch of the PostgreSQL 18.7 page on 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: SHARE lock, 'Acquired by CREATE INDEX (without CONCURRENTLY)', 'protects a table against concurrent data changes'; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (taken by VACUUM FULL among others) conflicts with every lock mode, so even plain SELECTs wait. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE list was read on the same page).

brief.situation: You are the database engineer on call at Fernhill Books, a fictional online bookshop. It is 11:00 on the first morning of the autumn sale. Since last night's release, sign-in has slowed from instant to about two seconds, and the application's database pool is nearly full. The sale email goes to 400,000 customers at 11:35, and sign-in traffic roughly triples when it lands. Find out why the lookup is slow, fix it without stopping orders, and show that it is fixed.
handover: Last night's release changed sign-in to match email addresses case-insensitively.
The customers table has 2.4 million rows, a primary key on id and a B-tree index on email. Orders insert and update customers rows (loyalty points) all day.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The incident keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, service or job and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

orders=# EXPLAIN SELECT id, email, name FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = 'reader@example.com';
                                    QUERY PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Scan using customers_lower_email_idx on customers  (cost=0.43..8.45 rows=1 width=41)
   Index Cond: (lower(email) = 'reader@example.com'::text)

orders=# EXPLAIN SELECT id, email, name FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = 'reader@example.com';
                              QUERY PLAN

 Seq Scan on customers  (cost=0.00..58840.00 rows=12000 width=41)
   Filter: (lower(email) = 'reader@example.com'::text)

then.finding: The plan is a Seq Scan with a Filter on lower(email): every row is read and tested. The index on email is not used, because it holds email, not lower(email).

then.finding: EXPLAIN ANALYZE: a sequential scan read 2.4 million rows and removed all but one with the filter, taking 1.8 s. The estimate (12,000 rows) is a guess for an expression it has no statistics on.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what the plan showed, why the existing index did not help, how you fixed it without stopping orders, and how you know it worked.

parts.label: Reading the plan
parts.criteria: Says EXPLAIN showed a Seq Scan with a Filter on lower(email) (and, with ANALYZE, millions of rows removed by the filter), and that a B-tree on email cannot answer a condition on lower(email).
parts.modelAnswer: EXPLAIN showed Seq Scan on customers with Filter: lower(email) = ...; EXPLAIN ANALYZE removed 2.4 million rows to return one in 1.8 s. The index stores email, not lower(email), so the planner cannot use it for that filter.

parts.label: The fix and its locks
parts.criteria: Builds an index on the expression lower(email), CONCURRENTLY so writes keep flowing; explains that a plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes and VACUUM FULL blocks everything, and neither ANALYZE nor enable_seqscan makes an index exist.
parts.modelAnswer: I built customers_lower_email_idx on (lower(email)) with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which does not block inserts and updates. A plain CREATE INDEX would have stopped orders for the build; VACUUM FULL would have locked out reads too.

parts.label: Verification
parts.criteria: Re-runs EXPLAIN to see an Index Scan with Index Cond on the new index and checks query time or pool use came down.
parts.modelAnswer: EXPLAIN now shows Index Scan using customers_lower_email_idx with Index Cond, mean time in pg_stat_statements fell to about 0.1 ms and the pool dropped to 4 busy.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written plan reading, fix and verification

expertPath.text: pg_stat_activity: the pool is full of the same sign-in lookup. pg_indexes: the only index besides the key is on email.
EXPLAIN (or EXPLAIN ANALYZE, a read): Seq Scan with Filter on lower(email), 2.4 million rows removed. The email index cannot serve lower(email).
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on (lower(email)); orders keep writing while it builds.
EXPLAIN shows Index Scan with Index Cond; pg_stat_statements mean time falls to about 0.1 ms. Close before 11:35.

fixed.headline: Good: fixed without stopping orders
fixed.body: The plan named the problem: a sequential scan filtering on an expression no index held. An expression index built concurrently fixed it with no lock on writes.

fixedGaps.headline: Fixed, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: Sign-in works. The criteria show what it cost: a guess instead of EXPLAIN, orders blocked by a plain CREATE INDEX, time, or no check afterward.

readsLocked.headline: Locked out the whole shop
readsLocked.body: VACUUM FULL takes the strongest lock there is and does not create an index. Read the plan first: it said Seq Scan with a Filter on lower(email).

poolExhausted.headline: The sale email arrived first
poolExhausted.body: With 35 minutes of warning, EXPLAIN and a concurrent expression index take about 15. Read the plan early; it names the fix.

stillSlow.headline: Closed too soon
stillSlow.body: Every sign-in still scanned the table. Statistics and session settings do not make an index exist.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Last night's release changed the filter to lower(email). The only index holds email, so EXPLAIN shows Seq Scan with Filter: lower(email) = ..., and EXPLAIN ANALYZE removes 2.4 million rows per lookup. An index on the expression lower(email) lets the planner use an Index Scan. Build it CONCURRENTLY so inserts and updates keep flowing (a plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes; VACUUM FULL blocks everything and fixes nothing here). Verify with EXPLAIN and query statistics before the 11:35 email.
